children: A consortium comprising QatarEnergy has signed a heads of agreement with Angola’s National Agency for Oil, Gas, and Biofuels (ANPG) for two offshore oil blocks in Angola.
The agreement includes Block 8 and 22, the state-backed energy company said in a post on X.
Other consortium partners are British oil and gas major Shell and Angola state-backed Sonangol E&P.
Under the deal, QatarEnergy will hold a 30 percent working interest, while Shell (the operator) will hold 50 percent and Sonangol will hold 20 percent in the two offshore blocks.
“The blocks are part of our international upstream exploration strategy and growth efforts,” said Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, CEO of QatarEnergy.

title: QatarEnergy to take stakes in 2 offshore blocks in Angola
